description: dataflow-op-lifecycle differential chain over EPLDataflowAPIOpLifecycle operator lifecycle stages (instantiated/property/open/next/onInput/close) observed across the forge, factory, and operator instances of the fixed Java oracle: type-event (ordinal 0) replays EPLDataflowTypeEvent as one compile-only compilation of create schema MySchema(key string, value int) plus @name('flow') create dataflow MyDataFlowOne MyCaptureOutputPortOp -> outstream<EventBean<MySchema>> {}, where the compile-time forge stores the declared output port and the single port-type record pins the declared event type name outstream=MySchema; flow-graph-source (ordinal 1) replays EPLDataflowFlowGraphSource with byte-exact @name('flow') create dataflow MyDataFlow @Name('Goodie') @Audit SupportGraphSource -> outstream<SupportBean> {propOne:'abc'} plus one replay-shape adaptation — a DefaultSupportCaptureOp(outstream) sink appended to the source-only graph because Go submissions require a connected edge — instantiated with dataFlowInstanceId id1 and dataFlowInstanceUserObject myobject, recording after instantiate the operator-context observables stage=instantiated, propOne=abc, dataflowName=MyDataFlow, instanceId=id1, userObject=myobject, operatorNumber=0, operatorName=SupportGraphSource, and after the blocking run() the stages open, next(numrows=0..2), close plus one capture record pinning the submitted rows E1 and E2; flow-graph-operator (ordinal 2) replays EPLDataflowFlowGraphOperator byte-exact with MyLineFeedSource injected through the operator provider over an abc/def iterator and the factory-realized SupportOperator recording stage=instantiated, stage=open, onInput=abc, onInput=def (each unwrapped from its single-element payload), stage=close; both replay cases end in the terminal state record state=complete after the instance reaches COMPLETE. Replay-shape adaptations frozen with the scouts: the compile-time forge-stage observables (initializeForge annotations and port maps) and the deploy-time factory-initialize observables (statementContext) are drained and discarded because the Go engine has no two-phase forge/factory split, and the post-compileDeploy empty-drain assertion of the third execution is a static-list mechanism artifact that is not represented.
